mappings.note: Neither looks nor intelligence, so no groom. Extraction of the father's stated worry.
Retrieves the unflattering reason she was sent. Extraction; the effect of the schooling is a separate outcome.
The hope of finding a friend on day one is the first step of the confidence LO-21 asks to be traced. Not LO-1: the item wants the feeling, not the fact.
'Different from the people at home' is LO-20's exact contrast -- what the teacher gives her that her family did not.
Why the parents accepted: otherwise she would never marry. Extraction of their reasoning.
The marriage fails on the dowry demand and her refusal. LO-22, not LO-1, because the refusal is the story's turn.
The bath, the oiled hair and the clean dress feel like better treatment only because she is a neglected child -- LO-19's starting point.
The teacher changing the course of her life. The core LO-20 item.
Asks why she first consented and then refused, and what that shows -- the refusal plus the growth that made it possible.
The return to 'Sulekha' marks the transformed girl, so LO-19; the naming itself is a literary device and no C-E2.3 outcome exists in this chapter, so the competency carries that half.
Carries the story's message to the girl-child scheme and a poster. The writer's message generalised; not LO-22, since Bholi's refusal is not the subject.
Names the teacher's encouragement as the lever, then asks the student to act on the same message. Both halves.
Girls' rights and human rights in general. The message, reaching well past the text; no LO covers a civics discussion.
Numberdar, Tehsildar, Pitaji as clues to the language and place. The chapter's setting item.
Bholi is the artist's work of art, the artist being the teacher. LO-20's metaphor as an MCQ.
Money as the dowry. Extraction.
Contempt in her eyes at the second lifting of the veil is the refusal beginning. Not LO-21: this is the act, not the growth.
Meaning of 'envious'. No LO in this frame covers word-level vocabulary, so the competency is cited.
Shop, house, bank balance -- his means, as the text gives them. Extraction.
Leaving school with a ray of hope is the first named turning point in the confidence arc.
Dress, oil and bath together, against a childhood of neglect. Same treatment as the short-answer version.
The mother's three reasons, all stated. Extraction.
Send his daughters to school. Extraction.
The house described as prosperous -- setting, and the irony that a prosperous home neglected her.
She began speaking at five. Extraction.
The fall from the cot. Extraction; smallpox is the distractor and a separate item.
Meaning of 'simpleton'. Vocabulary, so the competency -- although the word is her nickname.
Five thousand rupees. Extraction of the figure.
Kind and loving, on the first day. The teacher's manner, which is LO-20's subject.
Lakshmi is the cow. Extraction.
No new clothes, hair uncombed, nobody caring: the neglected child LO-19 begins from.
Seven children. Extraction.
Four daughters. Extraction.
Sulekha. Extraction of the name; what the name comes to mean is a separate item.
The village Numberdar. Extraction.
She spoke little because she was mimicked -- the silence that education later ends. LO-19's 'a person who can speak for herself', read backwards.
To open the girls' school. Extraction.
Names K.A. Abbas. Extraction.
The mother weeping at the idea of school. Her character, which the chapter returns to in a short answer.
Crying with fear is where the confidence arc starts, so LO-21 rather than recall.
They laughed at her stammer. Extraction.
The cow, goat and parrot on the wall. Extraction.
His age as the objection is the ground of her refusal. Not LO-1: the item asks the student to judge.
Asking for compensation on seeing her face is the greed her refusal answers.
Mean, greedy, coward -- her own words about him as she refuses. LO-22.
The teacher is the artist. Paired with the 'work of art' item; both belong to LO-20.
Bishamber Nath. Extraction.
Radha. Extraction.
Numberdar. Extraction, the same fact in a second stem.
Bholi alone was sent. Extraction; why only she is a separate short answer.
Two years old. Extraction.
'What transformation did education bring' is LO-19 word for word.
Pock-marks, stammer, simpleton: all three grounds of the discrimination LO-19 starts from.
Neither good-looking nor intelligent. Extraction of the stated worry.
The artist-and-masterpiece image explained. LO-20's teacher, at three marks.
Asks whether the refusal was possible without education -- the transformation and the refusal joined in one counterfactual.
Education's transformative role, directly. LO-19.
A personal response to her neglect, which is the condition LO-19 measures the change against. Not LO-20: the teacher is not yet in view.
The unequal match and her silence, then what should be done about it: the refusal's significance plus the message drawn out.
'Bholi was a neglected child. Explain.' -- LO-19's premise stated as the question.
The fall, the damage, the stammer and the nickname. Extraction of the chain.
Her promise to serve her parents and teach at her old school is what her refusal amounts to -- LO-22's 'what her refusal says'.
The garland thrown away and the veil cast off. The two acts of refusal.
Why the marriage did not happen: his demand, her refusal. LO-22.
Ramlal's wife as a mother. Character; not LO-20, which is about what the teacher supplied instead.
The teacher's patience on day one, and the confidence it produced -- the two outcomes meeting at the first turning point.
Pock-marks, no looks, no sense, the stammer -- the reasons, all stated. Extraction.
A third phrasing of the same question about the unaccustomed care. LO-19, as before.
Three daughters were already married. Extraction.
Bholi set beside her healthy, married sisters. Character by comparison, not a single retrievable fact.
The family's reputation before the school. Extraction of the stated reason.
The teacher's promise that she would one day be the most learned in the village. LO-20's patience, specifically.
The relatives' astonishment measures the distance she has travelled and lands on the refusal. Both outcomes.
The horse, goat, parrot and cow matched to things she knew. Extraction.
A diary entry on the girl child and the impact of education -- LO-19's theme, in the extended written form LO-3 measures.
A dialogue about discrimination today, with no reference to Bholi's own acts. The message, written at length, not LO-22.
A blog on educating the girl child and how it empowers her: LO-19's claim, argued at five marks.
A speech in Bholi's voice on being fearless requires the confidence arc and its turning points. LO-21, as writing.
Bishamber described, and why she refused him. LO-22 at five marks; not LO-4, since he is only the occasion for the refusal.
Her promise to her father, and what made her aware of her rights -- the refusal's meaning plus the teacher who made it possible.
'Dumb cow' to fearless girl is the arc, and the answer is the teacher's affection. LO-21 with LO-20 as the cause.
Social evils and what the student can contribute. The message, at length; the stand Bholi took is the premise, not the task.
A character sketch of Bholi together with the teacher's role. Character plus LO-20, in the long-answer form.
Three sub-items retrieve from the extract about the Tehsildar's visit; the fourth asks why the school's opening mattered to Bholi, which is LO-19's hinge.
